title: American Innovation $1 Coin Act
official_summary:
American Innovation $1 Coin Act

(Sec. 2) This bill directs the Department of the Treasury, over a 14-year period beginning in 2019, to mint and issue "American Innovation" $1 coins commemorating innovation and innovators from each state, each U.S. territory, and the District of Columbia.

Such coins shall be issued in the order in which the states ratified the Constitution or were admitted into the Union. After all such coins are issued, coins shall be issued for the District of Columbia and the territories.

Treasury shall issue four coins per year until a coin has been issued for each jurisdiction.

Neither the bust of any person nor the portrait of any living person may be included in the design of the coins.

The bill instructs Interior to continue to mint and issue $1 coins honoring Native Americans and their contributions.

summary.headline: This law directs the Treasury to mint a series of $1 coins honoring innovation from each state, territory, and the District of Columbia.
summary.what_it_does: Starting in 2019, the Treasury Department was directed to issue four American Innovation $1 coins per year over about 14 years, one for each state, U.S. territory, and the District of Columbia. Coins follow the order in which states ratified the Constitution or joined the Union, with D.C. and the territories issued after the states. Coin designs may not show a bust of any person or a portrait of any living person. The Interior Department was told to keep minting its separate $1 coins honoring Native Americans.

who_it_affects.group: People who collect or use U.S. coins
who_it_affects.how: They will receive a new series of $1 coins with state-based designs over the program's run.

who_it_affects.group: The U.S. Mint and Treasury Department
who_it_affects.how: They must produce and issue the coins on the set schedule and follow the design limits in the law.
It must continue minting its $1 coins that honor Native Americans and their contributions.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Signed into law July 20, 2018, with the coin program set to begin in 2019 and run for about 14 years.
